subject.title: resolveCliAuthEpoch invalidates every live CLI session when local credential source-of-storage flips, even though identity is unchanged

question: For Claude CLI sessions with a selected OpenClaw auth profile, should the auth epoch track stable credential identity rather than whether local credential storage is currently readable or present?
rationale: The code fix is small, but the intended security/session boundary is not purely mechanical: one choice avoids spurious context loss, while another keeps fail-closed invalidation for absent or unreadable local auth state.

options.title: Use profile identity when present
options.body: When a selected auth-profile credential exists, make it the canonical epoch identity and use the local Claude CLI fingerprint only for bootstrap/no-profile cases, preserving real profile identity changes.

options.title: Keep host credential as owner
options.body: Continue treating local Claude CLI credential presence as authoritative, accepting same-identity resets as the cost of fail-closed logout or unreadable-state detection.

options.title: Adopt host-only plus explicit absence policy
options.body: Use the host-only backend direction only if it also defines how file absence versus keychain/file source flips are distinguished from real logout.

recommendation.title: Use profile identity when present
recommendation.body: When a selected auth-profile credential exists, make it the canonical epoch identity and use the local Claude CLI fingerprint only for bootstrap/no-profile cases, preserving real profile identity changes.

likelyOwner.reason: The central auth-epoch invalidation behavior appears to originate in Peter Steinberger's `e5023cc141e2` commit, and this decision needs the same session/auth boundary ownership.
